solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Where cars wait — a road is normal

parts.note: a taxi rank or car stand is a place where cars wait
on maps and street signs road is shortened to RD

explanation.surface: A driver muses that a road with a queue of waiting cars is just the usual state of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something standard is the usual or ordinary kind, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Star cricketer, that man Brown?

definitions.note: a verb here, to go brown in the sun

parts.note: the Sun is a star
a bat is a batsman in cricket
he is that man

explanation.surface: Is the star cricketer a man called Brown?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname; it is the verb meaning to tan.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in the sun to tan is how you brown your skin; the question mark flags the verb sense.

clue.text: Worry gangster has got in

indicators.note: the word gangster has the answer's letters inside it

explanation.surface: Someone frets because a gangster has broken in.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is anxious dread, a heavier word for worry.

clue.text: Tied in factories with change leading to a loss of living things

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Industrial change linked to the death of wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: When land turns to desert its plants and animals die off, so life is lost.

clue.text: Turn on again and relax with creative activity

parts.note: to relax is to rest
art is creative work

explanation.surface: Advice to switch back on by relaxing with a hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart a machine is to switch it on once more after stopping.

clue.text: Location for play people without exception remember

parts.note: the rec is the recreation ground, a public park for games
everyone without exception is all

explanation.surface: Everyone is urged to remember a particular playground.
explanation.walkthrough: REC, short for recreation ground, is everyday British for a local park with pitches and swings.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall a memory is to bring it back to mind, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Banning of former contact

parts.note: ex means former
being in contact is being in communication

explanation.surface: A ban on someone who used to be a contact.
explanation.definitionFit: The church's formal exclusion of a member is a ban from its sacraments.

clue.text: Where people grow things for sharing

definitions.meaning: a rented garden plot for growing vegetables
a share-out or apportioning of something

explanation.surface: Plots where people garden and swap produce.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain these are small council-rented plots for growing vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a vegetable plot and an apportioned share.

clue.text: See new sign of agreement over City

parts.note: lo means look or see, as in lo and behold

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upward, read backwards

parts.note: a nod signals agreement

explanation.surface: Instructions to look for a new nod of approval over the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' also nods at the City of London, the financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: The British capital is a great city, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Animal in a cell — a second has been regularly raised

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read from bottom to top
regularly takes every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: A prisoner in a cell is promoted for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks ABE from HAS BEEN, and 'raised' turns it to EBA.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a single-celled organism, a whole animal in one cell.

clue.text: Drink that's good found in New England area?

indicators.note: a letter found in a region sits inside that region's letters

parts.note: New England lies in the north-east of the United States, NE plus US

explanation.surface: A question about whether a good drink can be found in New England.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus is an old-fashioned hot drink of port or sherry with sugar and spice.

clue.text: Lions come running _;_ this is the end

indicators.note: lions running scatter, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dramatic warning that charging lions spell the finish for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed punctuation mark itself is the definition: 'this is the end' points at the mark that ends the wordplay, which the anagram of LIONS COME names.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed mark in the middle of the clue is exactly the punctuation the anagram spells out.

clue.text: American substitute porter, perhaps welcoming group of three visiting

indicators.note: a word welcoming others takes them in, so the beer surrounds the rest

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, an example of ale
a tern is a set of three, as in a lottery win on three numbers
someone visiting a friend is at their house, giving AT

explanation.surface: A beer drinker welcomes a visiting trio while an American stand-in waits.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage an alternate is a deputy or reserve who stands in for another, as on a jury.

clue.text: Second time to give recurring phrase

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
taken as written

explanation.surface: A request for a moment to repeat a slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto is a saying adopted as a rule and repeated, a recurring watchword.

clue.text: Musician with history including activity during the Blitz

indicators.note: one word including another holds it inside

parts.note: HIST is a common abbreviation of history
ARP, Air Raid Precautions, was the civil defence work during the German bombing of Britain

explanation.surface: A musician with a wartime past, perhaps playing through the London bombing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blitz was the German bombing of British cities in 1940-41; ARP wardens enforced the blackout.
explanation.definitionFit: A harp player is one kind of musician, an example of the class.

clue.text: Get angry about blasted Margo's fuss

indicators.note: the verb goes about the jumbled name, surrounding it

parts.note: to rile is to make angry; here read as getting worked up

indicators.note: blasted means blown apart, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name Margo; the apostrophe-s is a link meaning has

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper over Margo's wretched carry-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, tiresome procedure, a lot of fuss.

clue.text: Cross at hosts for displaying charm

indicators.note: a word that hosts another contains it, so the letters of at surround the animal

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

explanation.surface: An angry host showing off his charm to guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, but it is the hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a trinket worn to ward off harm, a lucky charm.

clue.text: Biscuits or nuts

definitions.meaning: thin dry savoury biscuits, often eaten with cheese

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both savoury wafers and, colloquially, insane.

clue.text: Getting on? That's not about getting on

indicators.note: not about means the short word for about is taken away

parts.note: two people getting on are agreeing
RE is Latin-derived for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether growing old means failing to get along.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'getting on' phrases mean different things: the first is growing old, the second getting along with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone getting on in years is growing old, a common idiom.

clue.text: Casual chat and drink after work with son

indicators.note: the drink comes after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: a machine that works goes
to sip is to drink

explanation.surface: A natter over a drink with your boy once work is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip is idle talk about other people, light chatter.

clue.text: Writer of plays about a person like Vermeer

indicators.note: the playwright's name goes about the letter, surrounding it

parts.note: Harold Pinter was a British playwright

explanation.surface: A playwright writing about an artist such as Vermeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermeer was a Dutch master of oils, so he is an example of an artist with a brush.

clue.text: Clothing caught by épée awfully near point

indicators.note: something caught by another is held inside it
awfully signals the letters of the sword are mangled

parts.note: the fencing sword, letters without accents
a rig is an outfit of clothing

explanation.surface: A fencer's kit is snagged by a badly wielded sword.
explanation.definitionFit: Perigee is the point of an orbit nearest the Earth.

clue.text: Important one goes through papers?

definitions.meaning: a wire fastener pushed through sheets to hold them together

explanation.surface: A key official goes through the documents.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for chief and the small clip punched through paper.

clue.text: Trip abroad, oddly to see what Pope wears

indicators.note: oddly means taking the first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A tourist travels abroad to see the papal headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal tiara is the triple crown traditionally worn by popes.

clue.text: Cutting rotten carcass with it

indicators.note: a rotten carcass falls apart, so the letters with it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A butcher slices into a putrid carcass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like a butcher's action; it is the adjective meaning hurtful.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting remark is a wounding one, much like a sarcastic jibe.

clue.text: Couple, the first on the wagon

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it
the first means only the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a wain is an old farm wagon

explanation.surface: A pair ride on top of the wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Twain is an old word for two, a pair.

clue.text: Concert one performs vocally is likely to turn out well

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
the Roman numeral I is one
to perform with the voice is to sing

explanation.surface: A singer at a concert seems set for a bright future.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are an annual summer series of classical concerts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A promising newcomer shows signs of future success.

clue.text: Picture latter half of a trip to Santiago?

indicators.note: the latter half keeps only the last five of the ten letters

parts.note: the walk to Santiago de Compostela is a famous religious journey, a pilgrimage

explanation.surface: A holiday snapshot from the end of a Spanish journey.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Go off former European Union? Nicest on the outside

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A political grumble about leaving the old EU, which looks nicer from outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeunt is the stage direction telling several actors to leave the stage.

clue.text: Write numbers in a chain

parts.note: to pen is to write
nines are numbers

explanation.surface: Instructions to write figures in a sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pennines are the range of hills running down northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain chain is a range, and this English range forms the country's backbone.
